title: What 500,000 Qantas Points Gets You in 2026
body:
What 500,000 Qantas Points gets you in 2026 is close to the whole reward menu. You can get a return First Class Classic Flight Reward to London at 498,800 points. A Business Class oneworld award around-the-world costs 365,800 points. The balance can also cover paired premium bookings for two travellers in the same cabin. With half a million points, the 2026 reward tables open up a wide range of premium redemption options. Availability remains an important consideration. Here is what the balance can unlock under the 2026 tables. We cover the First Class and long-haul bookings it reaches, options for two travellers, and ways to protect your points.
What 500,000 Qantas Points represent under the 2026 tables
Under the current tables, 500,000 points represents close to the full menu. Only the oneworld First Class award in its top band, at 523,200 points, prices beyond it. Classic Flight Rewards are priced per passenger according to fixed distance bands. Taxes, fees and carrier charges are added separately on top. The current tables are applied to bookings made from 5 August 2025. As a benchmark, Point Hacks’ December 2025 rewards points valuations update lists a Qantas Point at 1.6 cents. It adopts Australian Frequent Flyer’s quarterly valuations. This values a well spent 500,000 point balance at $8,000 of travel. The premium cabin redemptions below are where that benchmark is within reach. The margin is decided by the cash fare each booking replaces. The headline options as of September 2026, per passenger and excluding taxes, fees and carrier charges, compare like this.
Booking Qantas Points required Return First Class, Sydney to London 498,800 Return Business Class, Sydney to London 332,600 oneworld Classic Flight Reward, Business Class, up to 35,000 miles 365,800 Two oneworld Classic Flight Rewards, Economy, up to 35,000 miles 304,400 Return Business Class to Asia for two travellers, Qantas aircraft 328,400
The first class and long-haul business bookings the balance reaches
The headline booking at this level is First Class, and the table prices it plainly. A one-way First Class Classic Flight Reward is in the top distance band and costs 249,400 points. This band covers routes such as Sydney to London. The balance therefore covers a return booking. First Class reward availability is the main consideration rather than the price. Reward seats are capacity-controlled and are not guaranteed until booked. The premium cabins release unevenly, so booking rewards suits a traveller who plans around the seat rather than the date.
Business Class turns the same balance into more travel. A return Business Class booking to London costs 332,600 points, leaving 167,400 points to spare. That is more than a further return Business Class trip to Asia at 164,200 points. Alternatively, the Business Class oneworld Classic Flight Reward costs 365,800 points. It covers up to 35,000 return miles on at least two oneworld member airlines other than Qantas. The itinerary can include up to five stopovers across Asia, Europe and the Americas. For a traveller with flexible dates and enough time, the oneworld Business Class award provides a way to combine multiple destinations in one itinerary. At 365,800 points, it can cost less than separate London and Asian return bookings. The First Class return offers a different redemption option for travellers prioritising the cabin experience.
How one balance covers two travellers
For two travellers, the balance can cover both travellers because Classic Flight Rewards are priced per passenger. The tables apply the same pricing to each seat. Two return Economy oneworld awards in the top band cost 304,400 points combined. This leaves almost 200,000 points remaining for other redemptions. Two return Business Class trips to Asia cost 328,400 points. This applies to the 3,601-4,800 mile band on Qantas aircraft. Children aged 2 and older pay the full points price per passenger on reward bookings. Infants under 2 who do not occupy a seat travel without a points charge. They must travel alongside an adult on a reward booking. A family of three with a toddler therefore pays for two seats.
Warning: The value benchmark is a multi-step calculation used to compare these options
Multiply the balance by the 1.6-cent December 2025 valuation to set the yardstick. 500,000 points have a benchmark of $8,000
For a candidate booking, take the cash price of the same seats, subtract the taxes, fees and carrier charges payable on the reward, and divide by the points required
A First Class return that exceeds the benchmark delivers at least $8,000 in calculated travel value against the valuation. If it does not, the paired Business Class and oneworld options can spread the same points across multiple trips
How to protect a large balance while you plan
Protecting the balance means keeping the account active and allowing for future changes to the tables. Qantas Points require earning or redeeming activity at least once every 18 months. This is straightforward for anyone with a points-earning card or eligible partner activity. The rules sit alongside every other program in the points expiry policies round-up . The tables themselves are not fixed in stone. The current prices took effect on 5 August 2025, with increases across most premium bands. Emirates moved to its own table for bookings from 31 March 2026. Recheck any plan based on last year’s prices before redeeming your points.
Our guide to the best ways to spend Qantas Points shows how this balance compares with smaller balances. A balance this size usually takes years of deliberate earning. Rebuilding it starts with the top Qantas Points-earning credit cards and other ways to earn Qantas Points . Bank program transfer bonus promotions can also periodically add value to conversions.
Frequently asked questions
Is First Class realistically bookable with points, or only in theory? +
First Class Classic Flight Rewards are real but scarce. Reward seats are capacity-controlled, availability isn’t guaranteed until you book, and premium cabins release unevenly across routes and dates. Travellers with flexible dates and a habit of checking regularly are the ones who land the 498,800-point return.
Is a oneworld award better value than separate bookings? +
Usually, where the itinerary suits it. A simple return Economy booking to London costs 127,000 points, while the Economy oneworld award costs 152,200 points. This covers up to 35,000 return miles with multiple stopovers, so the extra 25,200 points can buy several additional cities. The award only works when reward seats exist on every leg, which is its real cost.
How long does it take to earn 500,000 Qantas Points? +
That depends entirely on the earning engine. Card earn rates, sign-up bonuses, introductory points offers on new cards released by meeting a minimum spend within a set window, and partner activity all contribute at different speeds. The guides linked above compare realistic paths rather than reducing them to one number.
Do the points lose value while I save toward a booking? +
They can, in the sense that the tables can rise while the balance stands still. The 5 August 2025 repricing lifted most premium cabin prices, and points earn no interest, so it’s best to hold a large balance with a target booking in mind and spend it when availability appears. The partner ecosystem keeps the account active along the way.
Fees, rates and figures quoted are correct at the time of publication and should be verified directly with each provider before acting on them.
